sections.html: The African sea catfish (Arius africanus), also known as the marine catfish, is a species of sea catfish in the family Ariidae. It was described by Albert Günther in 1867 and reaches a maximum standard length of 45 cm.
Africa: Pangani River, Tanzania and estuaries of Madagascar. Known from the lower to middle reaches of drainages along the western coast of Madagascar and Eastern Africa.
Coastal species found in tropical brackish and freshwater in Tanzania, Madagascar, and the Pangani River.
The diet of the African sea catfish consists of small finfish and invertebrates.

Etymology: The specific name africanus means "from Africa".

IUCN Red List: This species is assessed as Data Deficient as little is currently known regarding the status of subpopulations from throughout its range. More research is required (IUCN 2017).
